why:
The FAIL line's evidence holds up. It names concrete wrong builds that check out against the repository. Changing the default separator to /[\t,]/ works with split() in src/parse.js and still passes the printf proof. A build that always splits on tabs breaks the real 'cli' test in test/csv.test.js. It also gives a concrete pair of readings: an unspecified printf input with or without commas in cells.

The PASS line's evidence fails the criterion. It names a wrong build, "a README that only lists the flag name in passing", but never says why the line catches it. Instead it argues about a different build: "A README with no --tsv fails it." It then concedes "This isn't a substantive weakness." A passing mention arguably satisfies "README.md documents --tsv", so the evidence never shows the line catching the build it says it tried.
